data.title: yuki.sato@sunrise.test is missing DMARC
data.group_title: {count} sending domains are missing authentication records
data.detail: The sending domain for yuki.sato@sunrise.test has no valid DMARC record. Google's bulk sender rules require SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to be aligned, so unauthenticated cold mail is filtered on arrival regardless of how good the copy is.
data.remedy: Add the missing DNS records at the domain's registrar, then re-check the domain from the mailbox to clear it immediately. This is the highest-leverage deliverability fix available and it costs nothing.
steps: Open your DNS provider for the domain this mailbox sends from. The records to add are below, ready to paste.
Add the DMARC record as a TXT record at the _dmarc host. It starts at p=none, which monitors without affecting delivery; tighten it to quarantine once a few weeks of reports look clean.
Give DNS up to a few hours to propagate. Most providers are much faster.
Send yourself a test message and check the headers show a pass for each record. Warmbly re-checks the domain on its own schedule and this clears itself once it does.

data.title: 3 contacts who unsubscribed are still in Sunrise Q3 launch outreach
data.group_title: {count} campaigns still have unsubscribed contacts enrolled
data.detail: 3 contacts in Sunrise Q3 launch outreach have unsubscribed but are still enrolled. Mailing someone who opted out is the fastest way to earn a spam complaint, and in several jurisdictions it is not merely impolite.
data.remedy: Remove them from the campaign. If they are still receiving mail, that is a routing problem worth understanding before anything else in this campaign.
steps: Open the campaign's contacts and filter to unsubscribed.
Remove them from the campaign. Suppression stops future sends, but leaving them enrolled keeps the campaign reporting an audience it must not mail.
Check whether any of them were sent to after they unsubscribed. If so, stop the campaign: that is a routing problem, and every further send compounds it.
Check where the list came from. Unsubscribed contacts reappearing usually means a re-import overwrote their status.

data.title: liam.walsh@sunrise.test is bouncing 4.5% of its sends
data.group_title: {count} mailboxes are bouncing too much mail
data.detail: 69 of 1526 sends from liam.walsh@sunrise.test bounced in the last 30 days. Amazon SES asks senders to stay under 5% and can pause sending at 10%; mailbox providers read a high bounce rate as a sender who does not know who they are mailing.
data.remedy: This is a list problem, not a mailbox problem. Verify the contacts in the campaigns this mailbox sends for before sending more, and remove the domains that bounce repeatedly.
steps: Pause the campaigns this mailbox sends for, so the rate stops climbing while you work.
Open Contacts and filter to the lists those campaigns use.
Run verification on the list, or re-import it from a verified source.
Delete or suppress every address that hard-bounced. Those never come back.
Resume sending, and watch the bounce rate on this page for a few days before raising volume again.

data.title: Opener reads like bulk mail
data.group_title: {count} steps read like bulk mail
data.detail: Opener uses "act now", "congratulations", "double your", "free trial", "guarantee", "limited time", "no obligation", "no strings attached", "once in a lifetime", "risk free", "this is not spam" and "100% free". Filters weight these phrases, but the bigger cost is that they make the message read as something nobody wrote to anyone in particular.
data.remedy: Rewrite those lines in the words you would use in a one-to-one email to this person. If a phrase would be strange to say out loud, it is strange to read.

data.title: Opener has copy that will not render
data.group_title: {count} steps have copy that will not render
data.detail: The body and plain-text body in Opener cannot be parsed as a template (line 1: unexpected EOF). Sending does not fail on this: it falls back to plain replacement, so conditionals and merge variables go out to the recipient as literal text.
data.remedy: Fix the template syntax. Check that every {{if}} has a matching {{end}}, that quotes are balanced, and that field names have no stray characters.
steps: Open the campaign and go to Opener.
The parser stopped here: line 1: unexpected EOF.
Every {{if}} and {{range}} needs its own {{end}}. A missing {{end}} is the most common cause and the error usually points past it, not at it.
Write a field with a leading dot, like {{.FirstName}}; the first_name and firstName spellings of built-in fields work too. A custom field is {{.city}}, or {{index . "city"}}.
Save, then use the preview to check it renders against a real contact rather than trusting that it looks right.

data.title: 25.0% of Q4 outbound (first draft) is shared inboxes
data.group_title: {count} campaigns are mailing mostly shared inboxes
data.detail: 25.0% of the 160 contacts in Q4 outbound (first draft) are addresses like info@ or sales@. Shared inboxes rarely reply, are usually read by someone with no interest in the offer, and complain at a higher rate than a named recipient does.
data.remedy: Filter role addresses out of the list and find the named person instead. A smaller list of real people outperforms a larger one of shared inboxes on every metric that matters.

data.title: The first email in Q4 outbound (first draft) has 4 links
data.group_title: {count} first emails carry too many links
data.detail: Opener carries 4 links in a first-touch email. Filters treat link-heavy first contact as a bulk signal, and a reader with four things to click does none of them.
data.remedy: Keep one link, or none. The goal of a first email is a reply, not a click.

data.title: The subject line in Opener is stacked with exclamation marks
data.group_title: {count} subject lines shout
data.detail: The subject "DON'T MISS OUT!! Our LIMITED TIME offer for your team is closing soon!!" is stacked with exclamation marks. Filters weight this as a bulk-mail marker, and a person reads it as shouting from a stranger.
data.remedy: Write it the way you would write to one person: sentence case, no exclamation marks.

data.title: 3 contacts who unsubscribed are still in Sunrise Q3 launch outreach
data.group_title: {count} campaigns still have unsubscribed contacts enrolled
data.detail: 3 contacts in Sunrise Q3 launch outreach have unsubscribed but are still enrolled. Mailing someone who opted out is the fastest way to earn a spam complaint, and in several jurisdictions it is not merely impolite.
data.remedy: Remove them from the campaign. If they are still receiving mail, that is a routing problem worth understanding before anything else in this campaign.
steps: Open the campaign's contacts and filter to unsubscribed.
Remove them from the campaign. Suppression stops future sends, but leaving them enrolled keeps the campaign reporting an audience it must not mail.
Check whether any of them were sent to after they unsubscribed. If so, stop the campaign: that is a routing problem, and every further send compounds it.
Check where the list came from. Unsubscribed contacts reappearing usually means a re-import overwrote their status.

data.title: elena.voss@sunrise.test has 1 error that nobody has cleared
data.group_title: {count} mailboxes have errors nobody has cleared
data.detail: elena.voss@sunrise.test has 1 error from the last 7 days still unresolved while it is attached to a running campaign. Send and sync errors do not surface as failures in campaign reporting, so a mailbox in this state quietly delivers less than the campaign asked for.
data.remedy: Open the mailbox and work through the errors. Authentication failures usually mean a reconnect; rate-limit errors mean the provider is pushing back and the cap should come down.
steps: Open the mailbox and read the errors. They are grouped by kind, and the kind tells you the fix.
Authentication or credential errors mean a reconnect. An expired OAuth token or a changed password will not recover on its own.
Rate-limit or throttling errors mean the provider is pushing back. Lower the daily cap and widen the send gap rather than retrying into it.
Connection or timeout errors are usually the host or port. Check them against your provider's current documented values.
Once the cause is fixed, the errors stop accumulating and this clears on the next check.

data.label: Smartlead

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Use the main account's key, not a client key, to see every client.

data.key_help: In Smartlead, click your profile icon, open Settings and copy the key from the API Keys section.
notes: Each Smartlead client becomes its own workspace.
SMTP mailboxes come over with their passwords. Google and Microsoft mailboxes are signed in again.
Leads that are only in a lead list, outside every campaign, cannot be read through Smartlead's API.
Subsequences come over as separate campaigns, without the reply categories that moved leads into them.

data.label: Instantly

fields.label: API key
fields.help: An API V2 key with the all:read scope.

data.key_help: In Instantly, open Settings, then Integrations, then API Keys, and create a key with the all:read scope.
notes: Each Instantly key reads one workspace. An admin workspace key also reads the sub workspaces in its workspace group; add a key for every other workspace.
Instantly does not return mailbox passwords, so custom SMTP and IMAP mailboxes are asked for again.
Subsequences and Liquid conditions are not brought over.

data.label: lemlist
data.key_help: In lemlist, open Settings, then Integrations, and generate an API key.
notes: Each lemlist team has its own API key, so an agency adds one key per client team.
Only email steps are brought over. LinkedIn, call, WhatsApp, manual task and condition steps are listed so you can rebuild them.
Mailbox passwords are not available through the lemlist API, so each mailbox is connected again in Warmbly.
Unsubscribed LinkedIn URLs and phone numbers are not brought over, only addresses and domains.

data.label: Reply.io

fields.label: API key
fields.help: A personal or Team key. The key needs read access to contacts, sequences and channels.

data.key_help: In Reply.io, open Settings, then API Key, and create or copy a key.
notes: A Reply.io key reads one team, so an agency adds one key per client team. Organization keys are not supported.
Only email steps are brought over. LinkedIn, call, SMS, WhatsApp, task and condition steps are listed so you can rebuild them.
Mailbox passwords are not available through the Reply.io API, so each mailbox is connected again in Warmbly.
Reply.io's own global blacklist rules are not brought over, only your team's.

data.label: Woodpecker

fields.label: API key
fields.help: An agency HQ key reads every active client account.

data.key_help: In Woodpecker, open Add-ons, then API & Integrations, then API keys, and create a key.
notes: The key needs Woodpecker's API keys add-on.
LinkedIn steps are not brought over.
Woodpecker's API cannot read campaigns with IF conditions, a scheduled start or manual task steps, so their emails are not brought over.
Mailbox passwords are not available through the API, so SMTP mailboxes are connected again in Warmbly.
Templates refer to custom snippets by number (snippet_1 to snippet_15), as Woodpecker's API returns them.
Wildcard domain patterns in the blacklist are not brought over.

data.label: Mailshake
data.key_help: In Mailshake, open Extensions, then API, and create a key.
notes: Mailshake's API returns each email's subject but not its body, delay or sending hours, so campaigns need their emails written before they start.
Drip and on-click emails are not brought over.
The unsubscribe list cannot be read through Mailshake's API; export it in Mailshake and upload the CSV.
Senders are connected again in Warmbly.
Mailshake meters its API by the hour, so a large team can take a few hours to read.

data.label: Saleshandy
data.key_help: In Saleshandy, open Settings, then API Keys, and generate a key.
notes: Saleshandy's API does not say which prospects are in a sequence, so prospects come over as contacts and are not enrolled in the imported campaigns.
Prospects belong to the whole Saleshandy account, so they are imported into the account's own workspace, not a client's.
Every do-not-contact list is applied to each workspace.
Mailbox passwords are not available through the API, so each mailbox is connected again.
LinkedIn, call, WhatsApp and task steps are not brought over.

data.label: Snov.io
data.key_help: In Snov.io, open Account settings, then API, and copy the client ID and secret.
notes: LinkedIn steps are not brought over.
Where a sequence branches on a condition, only the path for leads who did not meet it is brought over.
Snov.io's prospect lists hold names and addresses only, so company, job title and custom fields are not brought over.
Snov.io does not report how many emails a lead was sent, so a lead part way through a campaign cannot continue where it left off.
Mailbox passwords are not available through the API, so each mailbox is connected again.
Snov.io allows 60 API requests a minute, so a large account takes a while to read.

data.label: Apollo

fields.label: API key
fields.help: A master key, or a key allowed to search sequences, contacts, outreach emails, email accounts, schedules and custom fields.

data.key_help: In Apollo, open Settings, then Integrations, then API Keys, and create a master key (or a scoped key with the sequence, contact and email account endpoints).
notes: Apollo's API does not return a sequence's steps or email copy, so sequences come over with their settings and their emails are written again in Warmbly.
Apollo mailboxes are linked Google or Microsoft accounts, so each one is connected again in Warmbly.
Apollo has no readable blocklist. Contacts marked unsubscribed in Apollo come over unsubscribed.
Apollo's contact search stops at 50,000 contacts, so a larger account brings over the first 50,000.

data.label: QuickMail

fields.label: API key
fields.help: An agency API key; the plan needs API access.

data.key_help: In QuickMail, open your agency settings, find API Keys and create a key; API access has to be included in your plan.
notes: One QuickMail key reads every workspace in the agency.
QuickMail does not return mailbox passwords, so every inbox is connected again in Warmbly.
QuickMail's API does not say which workspace an inbox belongs to, so the agency's inboxes are listed for every workspace.
QuickMail's API does not return a campaign's sending schedule, inboxes or tracking settings; set them on the imported campaign.
QuickMail's API does not say how far each lead got in a campaign, so leads already in a campaign are restarted or skipped, never continued.
LinkedIn, call, task, SMS, Slack, webhook and checkpoint steps, Liquid conditions and domain-level Do Not Contact entries are not brought over.
